name: Canada

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 15,634,410 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 8,788,700 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). World Bank AG.SRF.TOTL.K2 for Canada reads 15,634,410 km2, inconsistent with every other source, so mid/high use the CIA Factbook total 9,984,670 km2 (land 9,093,507 + water 891,163); low is World Bank land area.

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 41,651,653). Low/high +/-1% for 2026 change and census revision. Everything inside ne:CAN.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2025 p.31 as quoted: 62,300 active. CIA Factbook 2025 gives ~75,000 (high); low allows for the trained-effective-strength shortfall DND has reported since 2022. World Bank MS.MIL.TOTL.P1 72,000 (2020).

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2025: 29,100 reserves (Primary Reserve plus Rangers etc.). Low is a Primary-Reserve-only paid-strength allowance; high an educated allowance for Supplementary Reserve recall.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 62,300 (IISS 2025) minus infantry P roles (3,500 + 3,000). Covers RCN (~8,400), RCAF (~12,000), armour/artillery/engineer crews, logistics, staff and the special-operations support element.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to Canada in WWII (about 1.1 million served from ~11.5 million people, ~9.5%); scaled down for an all-volunteer force with a small reserve and little stored equipment. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanized infantry personnel: 6 Regular Force LAV 6.0 battalions (PPCLI, RCR, R22eR 1st and 3rd/2nd battalions) x ~550 riflemen. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Canadian_Army)

quality.note: Rubric 0.75 band minus: LAV 6.0 mechanized infantry, Spike LR and Carl Gustaf; light on organic air defence.

training.note: Rubric 0.75 professional standing force; NATO eFP framework nation in Latvia.

count.note: Educated guess. Light battalions (3) plus CANSOFCOM (JTF2, CSOR) operators. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Canadian_Army)

training.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: special forces are elite long-service professionals; Afghanistan combat experience.

count.note: Equipment list: Leopard 2A6M/2A6M CAN 20 + Leopard 2A4/2A4M 54 = 74 after 8 donated to Ukraine (2023). 42 of the 2A4s are kept for training. High adds the Leopard 2-based ARV/AEV hulls not counted.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75 band minus: Leopard 2A6M is a contemporary tank; 2A4 training fleet is dated; no active protection.

training.note: Rubric 0.75 band minus: single tank regiment (LdSH(RC)), limited live-fire time.

count.note: Equipment list: LAV 6.0 616 + TLAV/M113 73 + Bison 155 + Coyote 56 + LAV 6.0 ACSV 128 delivered by Oct 2025 = 1,028. TAPV (500 armoured patrol vehicles) excluded as light protected mobility. Low allows for Bison/Coyote/TLAV retirements as ACSVs arrive.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75 band minus: LAV 6.0 is a modern wheeled IFV with 25 mm cannon; no tracked IFV.

training.note: Rubric 0.75 professional standing force; NATO eFP framework nation in Latvia.

count.note: M777 155 mm 33 (4 of 37 donated to Ukraine). High adds LG1 Mk II 105 mm 28; C3 105 mm (93) is a training/avalanche-control gun and excluded. HIMARS (26) contracted Jan 2026, production confirmed Apr 2026, none in service.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: M777 with Excalibur is good but there is no self-propelled or rocket artillery yet.

training.note: Rubric 0.75 professional standing force; NATO eFP framework nation in Latvia.

count.note: RCAF article: 85 CF-188 Hornets in service as of 2025 (103 in inventory: 72 CF-188A + 31 CF-188B). High adds the first 4 F-35A due in 2026 (88 ordered).

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: upgraded legacy F/A-18 Hornet; F-35A only arriving.

training.note: Rubric 0.75 band minus: NORAD/NATO standard, but CBC (Mar 2025) reported only ~40% of the RCAF inventory ready for action and a pilot shortage.

count.note: RCAF article: CH-146 Griffon 85 (2024) + CH-147F Chinook 14 (2025) + CH-148 Cyclone 27 + CH-149 Cormorant 13 (2023) = 139. No attack helicopters.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Chinook F and Cyclone modern, Griffon is a 1990s utility type.

count.note: Group 2+ UAVs: the 11 MQ-9B ordered in 2024 enter service from 2028 (RCAF article). Mid/high is an educated allowance for leased/contracted ISR UAVs and Army tactical systems; Canada fields no Group 3+ fleet of its own in 2026.

RCN article: 12 Halifax-class frigates (backbone of the fleet). Convention: ships_major = carriers/LHD + cruisers + destroyers + frigates. River-class destroyers not yet in service. Low allows for one hull in long refit.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Halifax-class mid-life modernized (HCM) 1990s frigates with ESSM/Harpoon; no area air defence.

training.note: Rubric 0.75 professional standing force; NATO eFP framework nation in Latvia.

count.note: RCN article: Harry DeWolf-class Arctic/offshore patrol vessels 5 + Kingston-class coastal defence vessels 4 = 9. High adds the Orca-class training tenders (8, not combatants) partially.

training.note: Rubric 0.75 professional standing force; NATO eFP framework nation in Latvia.

count.note: RCN article: 4 Victoria-class (ex-RN Upholder) submarines. Low reflects chronic availability: often only one boat operational (RCN commander, Jan 2026, BNN Bloomberg as cited).

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: 1980s design, poor availability; replacement (CPSP) not yet selected.

count.note: Equipment list: only RBS 70 NG MANPADS (unspecified number, from 2024) and counter-UAS systems bought for the Latvia brigade; no medium-range SAM. Counted as ~2 batteries; educated conversion.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75 (trained staff system, proven commanders) slightly discounted: NATO-integrated staff, led Kandahar task force 2006-11 and leads the Latvia multinational brigade; no corps-level command since Korea.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.75: professional regiments with strong identity (PPCLI, R22eR, RCR); recruitment/retention crisis since 2022 discounts slightly.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5 average; higher for continental/Arctic defence alongside the US.

weapons.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Excalibur, Spike LR, AMRAAM/ESSM; HIMARS and F-35 contracted but not fielded; few loitering munitions.

armor.note: Anchor 9 composite armour (Leopard 2A6M); no active protection.

ships.note: Anchor 9: modernized Halifax frigates with Link 16; River-class (Type 26) not in service; aging submarines.

fortification.note: Anchor 9 hardened facilities; NORAD North Warning System radars; no layered ground air defence (anchor 10 not met).

logistics.note: Anchor 9-10: strategic airlift (5 CC-177, 17 CC-130J, CC-330 tankers), but almost no sealift of its own.

communications.note: Anchor 9-10: Link 16, NATO/NORAD C2, Five Eyes; military satcom via WGS partnership.

isr.note: Anchor 9-10: RADARSAT Constellation Mission, CP-140 Aurora, NORAD; persistent drone ISR (MQ-9B) only from 2028.

air.note: Between anchor 9 (1985 jets) and 10 (5th generation): CF-188 Hornet fleet; F-35A deliveries begin 2026.

cyber.note: Anchor 10 partly met: Communications Security Establishment (Five Eyes) with active cyber operations mandate since 2019.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. Rebased GDP 1,933,497,120,784 / population 41,651,653 = 46,421 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 2,415,361,799,855 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 1,933,497,120,784 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Series: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/CAN/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 1.63% of GDP in 2025. Low is 2023 (CIA Factbook 1.3%); high 2.0% is the 2025 estimate after Canada declared the NATO 2% target met for FY2025-26 (CIA Factbook).

industrialShare.note: asOf 2022: industry incl. construction 27.35% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS).

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. One of the largest net exporters of wheat, canola, pulses and beef; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 20,681,413 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 5.617% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 232,349. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. GDLS-Canada London (Ontario) builds LAV 6.0/ACSV and LAV for export (Saudi contract); wartime rate limited by components. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Canadian_Army)

ships_major.note: Educated guess. River-class destroyer construction at Irving Halifax only started; first hull not before 2030. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Canadian_Navy)

artillery.note: Educated guess. No domestic gun line; could assemble light guns or HIMARS kits only with US supply chain. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Canadian_Army)

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook as quoted: 1,042,300 km total (2020), of which 415,600 km paved and 626,700 km unpaved (mostly engineered gravel). Low is paved only.

railKm.note: asOf 2021: 48,150 route-km (World Bank IS.RRS.TOTL.KM); CIA Factbook 49,422 km (2021, high). Standard gauge, two transcontinental systems (CN, CPKC).

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 284 ports, 4 large + 14 medium = 18; key ports include Vancouver, Prince Rupert, Montreal, Halifax, Quebec, Saint John. Low counts only ports with naval/major container facilities.

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: 3,305 thousand DWT under the Canadian flag (2,909 thousand GT), largely Great Lakes lakers. High is an educated allowance for Canadian-owned foreign-flag tonnage.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Analogy to NATO mechanized brigade sustainment; Canada sustains a brigade in Latvia through allied host-nation support and strategic airlift.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules and donkeys (not from FAO data). Militarily irrelevant in 2026.

nuclearWarheads.note: Canada is a non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces. Hosts no nuclear weapons since 1984.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: familiar terrain, local supply and population support; high 1.3 because the Arctic/sub-Arctic climate and continental depth punish an invader not adapted to it.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 data with 2026 order of battle. doctrineId nato-european-2026: no Canada-specific profile exists; this is the closest NATO middle-power profile (expeditionary brigade inside allied formations). Population convention: everything inside ne:CAN (World Bank). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts from IISS Military Balance 2025 as quoted on Wikipedia and the Canadian Army equipment list, RCAF and RCN articles (Government of Canada fleet pages as cited there). ships_major = carriers/LHD + cruisers + destroyers + frigates; ships_minor = AOPV, coastal defence vessels; drones = Group 2+ UAVs only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Readiness is the main caveat: DND reported large personnel shortfalls and low aircraft availability in 2025. ~2,000 troops deployed in Latvia (CIA Factbook 2025). Coast Guard is civilian and excluded.
